description: MORPH TOWARD A LISTED HARMONIC FIELD: the single-input sibling of newmorph's 2-file morph - the sound's spectral peaks are gradually tuned toward the goal-peak frequencies listed in a text peaksfile (most prominent first; the output format of newmorph newmorph2 mode 1, or hand-written). Linear interpolation in time; submode 3 is the identical argv with timewise-cosinusoidal interpolation (verified running, distinct sha). Duration is STATIC (verified 1.5209 -> 1.5209, 2.0230 -> 2.0230 via pvoc synth round-trips). Unlike the 2-input newmorph modes, endmorph beyond the file's end is ACCEPTED (verified: endmorph 5 on a 1.5 s file runs - the morph simply never completes), and there is no stagger/attack constraint. -r randomises the goal peak frequencies - but is DETERMINISTIC on this build (two -r0.5 runs 1.3 s apart byte-identical; the random path has no live seed). All four positional parameters are scalar-only.
musical_use: Pull any sound toward a chosen resonant skeleton without ever loading a second input: harvest a peaksfile from a bell, a vowel, a chord (newmorph2 mode 1), or write one by hand with write_data_file(), then let the source's peaks glide onto those frequencies between startmorph and endmorph. Because the goal is just a frequency list, this is the cleanest way to 'morph toward harmony' - list a spectral chord and the sound tunes itself into it as it plays. exponent shapes the approach (< 1 arrives early and sits; > 1 drifts then locks late); an endmorph past the file's end leaves the morph forever incomplete - a perpetual approach that never quite lands. peakcnt controls how many of the file's listed goals are used; -r smears the goal frequencies for a detuned, less gridded landing (repeatable on this build). Use submode 3 when the motion should ease in and out instead of moving at constant rate.

peaksfile.description: Text file of goal-peak frequencies in Hz, one per line, most prominent first (write with write_data_file(), any extension except .brk, or produce with newmorph newmorph2 mode 1). Asking for more peaks (peakcnt) than the file lists is accepted (verified: peakcnt 8 against a 6-line file runs).

startmorph.description: Time at which the morph starts. Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 2 ... brkpnt_files not permitted.').

endmorph.description: Time at which the morph ends. May exceed the file's duration (accepted; the morph never completes) - unlike the 2-input newmorph modes. Scalar only (parameter 3).

exponent.description: Exponent of interpolation (CDP-enforced 0.02-50, refusal verbatim). 1 = constant-rate approach. Scalar only (parameter 4).

peakcnt.description: Number of most-prominent source peaks to move (CDP-enforced 1-16, refusal verbatim '(1.000000 to 16.000000)'). Scalar only (parameter 5).

rand.description: Randomisation of the goal peak frequencies (CDP-enforced 0-1, refusal '-r2' verbatim '(0.000000 to 1.000000)'). Output-changing but DETERMINISTIC on this build - two -r0.5 runs 1.3 s apart are byte-identical (no live seed); A/B variants are not available.

examples.description: Tune a sustained sound into a harvested resonance skeleton.
examples.expected_use: The source's six strongest peaks glide onto the listed frequencies between 0.3 s and 1.2 s; duration unchanged.

examples.description: Perpetual approach - endmorph beyond the file end.
examples.expected_use: The morph is still incomplete when the sound ends: an unresolved drift toward the target field.

known_issues: Duration static (verified two input lengths). Single-input entry despite living in the newmorph binary - the 'second sound' is the aux peaksfile.
endmorph beyond the file's end is legal here (verified) - the 2-input newmorph refusal 'end of interpolation is beyond end of one of soundfiles.' does NOT apply to newmorph2.
-r accepted and output-changing but deterministic on this build (no live seed; same osbind drand48-shim family as other CDP 'random' paths) - do not expect run-to-run variants.
peakcnt larger than the peaksfile's line count is accepted (verified 8 vs 6 lines).
Positional params 2-5 refuse breakpoint files (parameter-N refusals probed).
Progress spam and 'WARNING: failed to write PEAK data' on every run - harmless. Deterministic (byte-identical data chunks).
